narration: FinMate is a financial agent for international students living abroad. Students enter their own balances and review tuition and living costs. These are planning snapshots. FinMate is not a bank, and every payment shown here uses simulated funds.

Before planning tuition, the student checks the recipient, account, amount and deadline. Tuition Guardian compares those details with the previous reviewed invoice. A changed account requires a separate independent check. Document text never grants payment permission.

Here, the student needs to cover two thousand three hundred euros of tuition. Their yuan balance is slightly short after fees, and expected income is delayed. FinMate excludes that future income. The student explicitly permits pounds as a backup. The rebuilt plan explains the change, shows fees and arrival, and preserves the euro living reserve.

The exact payment review shows every account contribution, the university recipient, the invoice reference and the protected reserve. Preparing this draft has moved no money. Approval requires a separate confirmation and the student’s payment PIN.

Sensitive actions remain outside the language model’s authority. An expired quote must be rebuilt and reviewed again. An incorrect payment PIN is rejected. Changes to balances, invoice details or simulated rates also invalidate previous payment consent.

After explicit approval, the sandbox commits the contributions and tuition payment together. A receipt and audit record show the result. Retrying the same approved payment returns that receipt instead of paying twice.

The assistant supports English and Chinese explanations. Its affordability answer uses verified calculation results, with a clear distinction between the emergency buffer over sixty days and the separate living reserve protected at payment time. Translation does not change approval authority.

Exchange rate reference data shows the European Central Bank as its source, with an observation date and freshness status. It is information only. Provider quotes and execution remain simulated. FinMate’s evaluation records seventy two repeated live agent runs and one hundred twenty nine automated tests. A real student study is prepared, but has not yet been conducted.
